subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: According to Newton’s Second Law of Motion, the force acting on an object is directly proportional to:
options: Rate of change of linear momentum
Total kinetic energy possessed by the body
Total distance covered per unit time
explanation: Newton’s second law states that the force acting on a body is directly proportional to the rate of change of its linear momentum (F = dp/dt = ma).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 1: Laws of Motion, Section 1.3

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: When a lift/elevator is falling freely downward under gravity (acceleration a = g), the apparent weight of a person inside the lift becomes:
explanation: During free fall, the downward acceleration of the lift equals g (a = g). The apparent weight R = m(g - a) = m(g - g) = 0. This state is known as weightlessness.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 1: Laws of Motion, Section 1.9

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: According to Lord Rayleigh’s scattering law, the amount of scattering of light (S) is inversely proportional to which power of its wavelength (λ)?
explanation: Rayleigh’s scattering law states that the amount of scattering of light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of its wavelength: S ∝ 1/λ⁴.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 2: Optics, Section 2.2

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: Sir C.V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for his discovery of Raman Effect. The spectral lines with frequency lower than the incident frequency are termed as:
explanation: In the Raman scattering spectrum, spectral lines having frequency lower than incident radiation are called Stokes lines, whereas lines having frequency higher than incident radiation are called Anti-Stokes lines.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 2: Optics, Section 2.4

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: At Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP), what is the molar volume occupied by one mole of any ideal gas?
explanation: According to Avogadro’s law, at standard temperature and pressure (STP: 273 K and 1 atm), one mole of any ideal gas occupies a volume of 22.4 litres (or 22.4 × 10⁻³ m³).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 3: Thermal Physics, Section 3.2

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: According to Joule’s Law of Heating, the heat (H) produced in a resistor of resistance R carrying current I for time t is given by:
explanation: Joule’s law of heating states that heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of current (I²), resistance (R), and time (t): H = I²Rt.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 4: Electricity, Section 4.6

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: In which of the following conditions does the Doppler effect of sound NOT occur?
options: Source is in motion while listener is at rest
Both source and listener move with the same velocity in the same direction
Listener is in motion while source is at rest
Both source and listener move towards each other
explanation: When both source and listener move in the same direction with the same speed, their relative velocity is zero, so there is no apparent change in frequency (no Doppler effect).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 5: Acoustics, Section 5.6

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: Which radioisotope is widely utilized in medical diagnosis and treatment for thyroid gland abnormalities and cancer?
explanation: Radioactive Iodine-131 (I-131) is specifically used for diagnosing and treating thyroid gland disorders, including goitre and thyroid cancer.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 6: Nuclear Physics, Section 6.5

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: What is the effect of increasing temperature on the solubility of a gas dissolved in a liquid solvent?
explanation: The dissolution of gas in liquids is generally an exothermic process. As temperature increases, the kinetic energy of gas molecules increases, causing gas to escape, thereby reducing its solubility.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 9: Solutions, Section 9.3

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: The pH scale was introduced by S.P.L. Sorensen in 1909. What is the pH value of pure human blood under normal physiological conditions?
explanation: Normal blood pH in healthy humans is slightly alkaline, strictly maintained within the narrow range of 7.35 to 7.45 by buffer systems.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 10: Types of Chemical Reactions, Section 10.4

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: Which allotrope of carbon consists of carbon atoms arranged in soccer-ball-shaped cages, commonly known as Buckyballs?
explanation: Buckminsterfullerene (C60) consists of 60 carbon atoms joined in a spherical soccer-ball geometry with 20 hexagons and 12 pentagons.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 11: Carbon and its Compounds, Section 11.2

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: In eukaryotic plant cells, the light-independent dark reaction (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis takes place in which part of the chloroplast?
explanation: The light reaction occurs in the thylakoid membranes (grana), while the light-independent dark reaction (Calvin cycle) takes place in the fluid stroma containing necessary enzymes.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 12: Plant Anatomy and Physiology, Section 12.7

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: The salivary glands of the Indian cattle leech (Hirudinaria granulosa) secrete which potent anticoagulant that prevents blood clotting while feeding?
explanation: Leeches secrete the protein hirudin in their saliva, an anticoagulant that prevents the host’s blood from clotting during feeding.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 13: Structural Organisation of Animals, Section 13.2

subject: Biology
lessonTitle: Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: Which specialized nodal tissue in the human heart acts as the natural primary pacemaker that initiates the cardiac rhythm?
explanation: The Sinoatrial (SA) node located in the upper right wall of the right atrium is known as the natural pacemaker of the human heart as it generates rhythmic electrical impulses.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 14: Transportation and Circulation, Section 14.12

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: Which part of the human hindbrain is primarily responsible for maintaining posture, equilibrium, and coordinating voluntary muscle movements?
explanation: The cerebellum (part of hindbrain) coordinates voluntary motor movements, maintains balance, equilibrium, and muscular posture.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 15: Nervous System, Section 15.3

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: Which endocrine gland is designated as the "Master Gland" of the human body because its secretions regulate other endocrine glands?
explanation: The pituitary gland produces trophic hormones that stimulate and regulate the activity of other endocrine organs (thyroid, adrenals, gonads), hence called the master gland.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 16: Plant and Animal Hormones, Section 16.4

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: In Gregor Mendel’s classic dihybrid cross experiment on pea plants, what is the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation?
explanation: The phenotypic ratio obtained in Mendel’s dihybrid cross in the F2 generation is 9 (Round Yellow) : 3 (Round Green) : 3 (Wrinkled Yellow) : 1 (Wrinkled Green).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 18: Genetics, Section 18.2

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: The historic "Chipko Movement" for forest conservation originated in 1973 in Chamoli district of which Indian state?
explanation: The Chipko Movement originated in Reni village of Chamoli district, Uttarakhand (then part of Uttar Pradesh), led by Sunderlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 22: Environmental Management, Section 22.3

subject: Geography
topic: Physical Divisions of India & Northern Mountains
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: Which of the following longitudinal ranges is the highest and most continuous chain of the Himalayas, also known as the Greater Himalayas?
explanation: The Greater Himalayas or Himadri is the highest and most continuous range with an average height of 6,000 metres and includes peaks like Everest and Kanchenjunga.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 1, Section 1.2

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: Which peninsular river flows through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges and empties into the Arabian Sea?
explanation: The Narmada rises in the Amarkantak plateau and flows westward through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 1, Section 1.6

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: The sudden approach of the Southwest Monsoon accompanied by intense lightning and thunder in the first week of June along Kerala coast is termed as:
explanation: The sudden arrival of moisture-laden monsoon winds causing sudden violent downpours with thunder and lightning is called the "burst" or "break" of monsoon.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 2, Section 2.3

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: Which is the largest mangrove delta forest in the world, formed by the confluence of the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers?
explanation: The Sundarbans delta in West Bengal and Bangladesh, famous for Sundari trees and the Royal Bengal Tiger, is the world’s largest mangrove ecosystem.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 2, Section 2.5

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: Black soil, which is ideal for the cultivation of cotton, is derived from the weathering of which type of parent rock?
explanation: Black soil (Regur) is derived from the weathering of volcanic basaltic lava of the Deccan Trap and has high clay and moisture retention properties, making it ideal for cotton.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 3, Section 3.1

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: India’s first modern integrated iron and steel plant, TISCO, was established by J.N. Tata at Sakchi (Jamshedpur) in which year?
explanation: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established in 1907 at Sakchi (now Jamshedpur, Jharkhand) and commenced pig iron production in 1911.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 4, Section 4.3

subject: Geography
topic: Relief Features & Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India (Tamil Nadu)
question: Which prominent pass in the Western Ghats connects Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu with Palakkad in Kerala?
explanation: The Palghat Gap (about 30 km wide) is a major natural mountain pass in the Western Ghats connecting Coimbatore/Tiruppur with Palakkad and the Kerala coast.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 6, Section 6.2

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India (Tamil Nadu)
question: The river Cauvery originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri Hills of Kodagu (Coorg) in which state?
explanation: The river Cauvery originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu district in Karnataka at an altitude of 1,341 m before flowing into Tamil Nadu.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 6, Section 6.5

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India (Tamil Nadu)
question: Which city in Tamil Nadu is renowned as the "Detroit of Asia" due to its large automobile and automotive ancillary manufacturing base?
explanation: Chennai accounts for over 60% of India’s automotive exports and houses major global automakers (Hyundai, Ford, BMW, Renault-Nissan), earning it the title "Detroit of Asia".
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 7, Section 7.4

subject: History
lessonTitle: Early India: From Beginnings to Indus Civilisation
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: History & Culture of India
question: At which Harappan archaeological site was the world’s oldest excavated artificial dockyard and tidal port identified by S.R. Rao in 1957?
explanation: Lothal in Gujarat, located on the banks of the Bhogava river, possessed a brick-lined tidal dockyard connecting the Harappan civilization with Persian Gulf trade.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 History, Volume 1, Lesson 1, Section 1.5

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: History & Culture of India
question: In which famous Rock Edict does Emperor Ashoka describe his remorse and renunciation of warfare following the bloodshed of the Kalinga War (261 BCE)?
explanation: Major Rock Edict XIII gives a moving personal account of Ashoka’s remorse after the Kalinga war and his adoption of Dhamma Vijaya (conquest by righteousness) instead of Bheri Ghosha.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 History, Volume 1, Lesson 4, Section 4.3

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: History & Culture of India
question: The Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti), which records the military conquests and genealogy of Samudragupta, was composed by his court poet:
explanation: Harisena composed the 33-line Sanskrit eulogy (Prashasti) on the Allahabad Pillar inscribed in elegant Champu Kavya style praising Samudragupta.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 History, Volume 1, Lesson 5, Section 5.2

subject: History
lessonTitle: Socio-Religious Reform Movements in the 19th Century
topic: Brahmo Samaj & Raja Ram Mohan Roy
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: History & Culture of India
question: Under the advocacy of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, in which year did Governor-General Lord William Bentinck enact Regulation XVII prohibiting the practice of Sati?
explanation: Regulation XVII was promulgated on 4th December 1829 by Lord William Bentinck declaring the practice of Sati illegal and punishable as culpable homicide in Bengal.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 5, Section 5.1

subject: History
lessonTitle: Early Revolts Against British Rule in Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: History & Freedom Struggle
question: Where was the brave Poligar of Panchalankurichi, Veerapandiya Kattabomman, executed by hanging by the British in October 1799?
explanation: Veerapandiya Kattabomman was tried by Major Bannerman in front of fellow Poligars and hanged from a tamarind tree at Kayathar on 16th October 1799.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 6, Section 6.2

subject: History
lessonTitle: Early Revolts Against British Rule in Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: History & Freedom Struggle
question: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Madras Army whose controversial new dress regulations and agnatic turban orders triggered the Vellore Mutiny of 10 July 1806?
explanation: Sir John Cradock introduced new turban regulations banning religious caste marks on forehead, ear rings, and trimmed moustaches, which triggered the sepoy uprising at Vellore Fort.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 6, Section 6.4

subject: History
lessonTitle: Anti-Colonial Movements and Birth of Nationalism
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: The play "Nil Darpan" (The Mirror of Indigo), depicting the plight and torture of Bengal indigo peasants under European planters, was written by:
explanation: Dinabandhu Mitra authored the Bengali drama "Nil Darpan" in 1858–1859, which galvanized public consciousness and led to the Indigo Commission of 1860.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 7, Section 7.2

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Freedom Struggle in Tamil Nadu
question: During the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930, who organized and led the historic Salt Satyagraha march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu?
explanation: C. Rajagopalachari led 100 dedicated volunteers from Tiruchirappalli on 13 April 1930 and reached Vedaranyam on 28 April 1930 to manufacture salt and break the salt law.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 9, Section 9.3

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Social Transformation in Tamil Nadu
question: In which year did the Justice Party government in the Madras Presidency enact the historic Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act to regulate temple administration?
explanation: The Justice Party ministry passed the Hindu Religious Endowments Act in 1926 (Act II of 1927), enabling government-appointed boards to supervise temple wealth and curb irregularities.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.3

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Constitution)
question: Who was unanimously elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly of India on 11 December 1946?
explanation: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary president on 9 December 1946, and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.1

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Constitution)
question: Which three words were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976?
explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) introduced three words into the Preamble: "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity".
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.2

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Fundamental Rights)
question: Which Article of the Constitution of India was characterized by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the "Heart and Soul of the Constitution"?
explanation: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies (issuance of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari) without which fundamental rights are ineffective.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Polity
topic: President of India & Ordinance Making Power
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Union Executive)
question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the President empowered to promulgate Ordinances during the recess of Parliament?
explanation: Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate Ordinances when neither House of Parliament is in session. (Governor promulgates under Article 213).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.2

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Parliament)
question: What is the maximum time period within which the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha with or without recommendations?
explanation: Under Article 109, Rajya Sabha has 14 days to consider a Money Bill. If not returned within 14 days, the bill is deemed passed by both Houses in its original form.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.5

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (State Government)
question: Under Article 356 of the Indian Constitution, on whose report or satisfaction can the President impose President’s Rule in a State?
explanation: Article 356 allows the President to issue a proclamation imposing President’s Rule on receipt of a report from the Governor or if satisfied that governance cannot be carried on per Constitutional provisions.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 3, Section 3.2

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Federalism)
question: The Government of Tamil Nadu appointed the P.V. Rajamannar Committee in 1969 to examine and recommend reforms on which critical subject?
explanation: The DMK government headed by M. Karunanidhi constituted the 3-member Rajamannar Committee in 1969 to inquire into Centre-State relations and secure maximum autonomy for states.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Political Science, Lesson 5: Federalism, Section 5.4

subject: Polity
lessonTitle: Anti-Corruption Measures: Lokpal, Lokayukta, CVC & CBI
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Anti-Corruption)
question: Which was the first Indian state to pass and establish the institution of the Lokayukta through legislation in 1971?
explanation: Maharashtra was the first state to introduce the Lokayukta through the Maharashtra Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayuktas Act in 1971.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Political Science, Lesson 6: Administrative Machinery, Section 6.5

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (RTI)
question: Under the Right to Information Act 2005, within how many days must an aggrieved applicant file a First Appeal against the decision of the Public Information Officer (PIO)?
explanation: Under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act 2005, any person who does not receive a decision within 30 days may prefer an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Political Science, Lesson 7: Citizen Empowerment, Section 7.2

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Gross Domestic Product and Sectoral Contributions
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy
question: Which sector of the Indian economy is currently the largest contributor to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
explanation: The tertiary (services) sector—comprising banking, IT, transport, communication, and real estate—accounts for over 53% of India’s GDP.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 1, Section 1.2

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Government and Taxes: Fiscal Systems & GST
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Taxation)
question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was officially launched across India on which date via the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act?
explanation: GST, a destination-based unified indirect tax, officially came into effect across India from midnight on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act 2016.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 4, Section 4.3

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Tamil Nadu Economy
question: Which region in western Tamil Nadu is renowned as the "Textile Valley of Tamil Nadu" and contributes heavily to knitwear garment exports?
explanation: Tiruppur (known as Knit City / Dollar City) along with Coimbatore accounts for the largest chunk of cotton knitwear and yarn exports in India.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 5, Section 5.3

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Rural Development)
question: Under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA 2005), how many guaranteed days of wage employment per financial year are provided to rural households?
explanation: MGNREGA legally guarantees at least 100 days of unskilled wage employment per financial year to adult members of any rural household willing to do manual work.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 10: Rural Economy, Section 10.4

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Tamil Nadu Economy: Macro Performance & HDI
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Tamil Nadu Economy
question: Unlike the targeted PDS model adopted in most Indian states, Tamil Nadu uniquely operates which form of Public Distribution System?
explanation: Tamil Nadu uniquely practices a Universal Public Distribution System where all family ration cardholders are entitled to subsidized essential grains (including free rice), regardless of income criteria.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 11: Tamil Nadu Economy, Section 11.6

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Banking and Central Banking: Reserve Bank of India
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Banking)
question: What is the rate of interest at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends short-term liquidity to commercial banks against government securities called?
explanation: Repo (Repurchase Option) Rate is the key policy interest rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to scheduled commercial banks against eligible government securities.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Economics, Lesson 6: Banking, Section 6.4

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Economics of Development, Planning & NITI Aayog
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (NITI Aayog)
question: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was officially instituted to replace the erstwhile Planning Commission of India on:
explanation: NITI Aayog was established by a Cabinet resolution on 1st January 2015 as the premier policy think tank of the Government of India promoting cooperative federalism.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Economics, Lesson 11: Economics of Development and Planning, Section 11.5

subject: Ethics and Culture
lessonTitle: Indus Valley Civilisation and Dravidian Links
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: History & Culture of Tamil Nadu
question: Which prominent Finnish Indologist published extensive research proposing that the Indus script represents an ancient Proto-Dravidian language?
explanation: Prof. Asko Parpola (Deciphering the Indus Script) demonstrated through linguistic and structural analysis that Indus signs represent astronomical and Dravidian roots.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Ethics and Indian Culture, Lesson 2: Indus Civilization and Tamil Culture, Section 2.3

subject: Ethics and Culture
lessonTitle: Living Values in Tamil Literature (வாழ்வியல் நெறிகள்)
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Sangam Literature & Culture
question: In ancient Tamil Sangam poetry and Tolkappiyam, which Thinai (geographical landscape) is associated with the coastal seashore and the deity Varunan?
explanation: Under the Ainthinai system: Kurinji (Murugan/Hills), Mullai (Mayon/Forests), Marudham (Vendan/Fields), Neithal (Varunan/Seashore), and Palai (Kotravai/Arid).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Ethics and Indian Culture, Lesson 3, Section 3.2

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Dravidian Movement & Periyar
question: In May 1925, Thanthai Periyar E.V. Ramasamy launched which influential Tamil weekly journal as the official mouthpiece for the Self-Respect Movement?
explanation: Periyar started the Tamil weekly "Kudi Arasu" in May 1925 from Erode to advocate rationalism, anti-untouchability, and women’s liberation.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.4

subject: History
lessonTitle: The Dravidian Movement and Perarignar Anna
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Dravidian Movement & Anna
question: At the historic Salem Conference in August 1944, C.N. Annadurai passed a resolution officially renaming the South Indian Liberal Federation (Justice Party) as:
explanation: At the 1944 Salem Provincial Conference, the Justice Party was merged with the Self-Respect League and renamed "Dravida Kazhagam" under the leadership of Periyar.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.5

subject: History
lessonTitle: Pioneers of Freedom Struggle in Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Role of Tamil Nadu in Freedom Movement
question: Mahakavi Subramania Bharati served as the sub-editor of which famous Tamil nationalist daily newspaper started by G. Subramania Iyer in 1904?
explanation: Subramania Bharati joined "Swadesamitran" (founded by G. Subramania Iyer) as sub-editor in November 1904, where his fiery patriotic articles were first published.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 9, Section 9.1

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: Which of the following is the correct second equation of uniformly accelerated motion relating displacement (s), initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and time (t)?
explanation: The second equation of motion for uniform acceleration is s = ut + ½at², derived from the velocity-time relationship.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Term 1, Lesson 2: Motion, Section 2.5

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: Pascal’s Principle, which states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted undiminished in all directions, is the operating principle of:
explanation: Hydraulic brakes, hydraulic presses, and hydraulic lifts work on Pascal’s Law: pressure exerted at any point of an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Term 1, Lesson 3: Fluids, Section 3.4

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: What is the SI unit of electric potential difference (voltage)?
explanation: The SI unit of electric potential difference is the Volt (V), named after Alessandro Volta. One volt is equal to one joule per coulomb (1 V = 1 J/C).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Term 2, Lesson 4: Electric Current, Section 4.2

subject: Physics
topic: Fleming’s Left Hand Rule & Electric Motor
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: In Fleming’s Left Hand Rule used to determine the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, the middle finger points in the direction of:
explanation: In Fleming’s Left Hand Rule: the thumb represents Force/Motion, the forefinger represents the Magnetic Field, and the middle finger represents the Current.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Term 2, Lesson 5: Magnetism, Section 5.5

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: Henry Moseley proposed the Modern Periodic Law in 1913, stating that physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their:
explanation: Modern Periodic Law states that properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers (Z), replacing Mendeleev’s atomic mass basis.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Lesson 12: Periodic Classification, Section 12.2

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: Which natural organic acid is predominantly present in citrus fruits such as lemons and oranges?
explanation: Lemons and oranges contain citric acid; vinegar contains acetic acid, curd contains lactic acid, and tamarind contains tartaric acid.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Lesson 14: Acids, Bases and Salts, Section 14.1

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: Which organelle is designated as the "Powerhouse of the Cell" because it synthesizes ATP through cellular respiration?
explanation: Mitochondria produce cellular energy in the form of Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) via the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Lesson 18: Cell Biology, Section 18.3

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: Deficiency of Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) in the human diet leads to which clinical deficiency disease?
explanation: Deficiency of Vitamin C causes Scurvy, characterized by spongy and bleeding gums, delayed wound healing, and skin haemorrhages.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Lesson 21: Nutrition and Health, Section 21.4

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: The point on the Earth’s surface vertically directly above the underground focus (hypocentre) of an earthquake is termed as the:
explanation: The hypocentre (focus) is the point of origin inside the earth, and the point on the surface directly above it is called the Epicentre.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Social Science, Geography Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: In which layer of the Earth’s atmosphere is the protective Ozone layer (O3) primarily concentrated?
explanation: The ozone layer is concentrated in the Stratosphere between 15 km and 35 km altitude, absorbing harmful ultraviolet (UV) solar radiation.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Social Science, Geography Lesson 3, Section 3.2

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: The Indian Standard Meridian (82°30′ E longitude) passes through which city near Prayagraj (Allahabad)?
explanation: Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated based on the 82°30′ E longitude passing through Mirzapur near Prayagraj, which is UTC + 5:30 hours ahead of GMT.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 1, Section 1.1

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: The Golden Quadrilateral highway project with a total length of 5,846 km connects which four major metropolitan cities of India?
explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral super-highway connects the 4 mega cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata, managed by NHAI.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 5, Section 5.2

subject: Geography
topic: Wildlife Sanctuaries & Biosphere Reserves of TN
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India (Tamil Nadu)
question: Which was the first declared Biosphere Reserve in India (established in 1986), spanning parts of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka?
explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was established in 1986 as India’s first biosphere reserve, encompassing Mudumalai, Mukurthi, Wayanad, and Bandipur.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 6, Section 6.7

subject: History
lessonTitle: People Revolt: Poligar Rebellion & 1806 Vellore Mutiny
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: History of Tamil Nadu
question: Who was the trusted commander of Queen Velu Nachiyar’s women army wing (Udaiyal) who executed a suicide bombing attack on the British ammunition depot at Sivagangai?
explanation: Kuyili drenched herself in oil, set herself ablaze, and leapt into the British ammunition storehouse, destroying British munitions in 1780.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 4, Section 4.2

subject: History
lessonTitle: Anti-Colonial Movements and Birth of Nationalism
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: Who presided over the historic first session of the Indian National Congress held at Bombay in December 1885?
explanation: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee was elected president of the inaugural session of the Indian National Congress held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 7, Section 7.3

subject: History
lessonTitle: Anti-Colonial Movements and Birth of Nationalism
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: Which prominent early nationalist leader formulated the "Drain of Wealth" theory in his pioneering book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"?
explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji (the Grand Old Man of India) exposed how British rule drained millions of pounds of Indian wealth annually to Britain without economic return.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 7, Section 7.4

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: In protest against the horrific Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919, who renounced his British Knighthood?
explanation: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his British Knighthood in May 1919 with a stirring letter to the Viceroy expressing condemnation of the Amritsar massacre.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 8, Section 8.2

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Freedom Struggle in Tamil Nadu
question: Which patriotic nationalist leader established the "Bharat Ashram" at Papparapatti in Dharmapuri district to train youth for freedom struggle?
explanation: Subramania Siva established the Bharat Matha temple and Bharat Ashram at Papparapatti in Dharmapuri district to instill patriotic devotion among the youth.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 9, Section 9.2

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (DPSP)
question: The Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36–51) in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
explanation: DPSP was inspired by the Constitution of Ireland (which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.4

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Fundamental Duties)
question: Fundamental Duties were incorporated into Part IV-A (Article 51-A) of the Indian Constitution on the recommendation of which committee?
explanation: The Sardar Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties, which were enacted via the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.5

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Judiciary)
question: The concept of "Judicial Review", which empowers the Supreme Court and High Courts to strike down unconstitutional legislation, was adopted from:
explanation: Judicial Review in India is adopted from the United States constitutional jurisprudence (Marbury v. Madison).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.7

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Local Government)
question: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992, which permanent statutory body at the grassroots village level consists of all registered voters in the panchayat area?
explanation: Under Article 243-A, the Grama Sabha is the grassroots general assembly composed of all persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village panchayat.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Social Science, Civics Lesson 5, Section 5.3

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Food Security and Universal PDS in Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Food Security)
question: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was passed by the Parliament of India in which year to legally guarantee subsidized foodgrains to eligible beneficiaries?
explanation: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in September 2013, covering up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 3, Section 3.2

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Demography)
question: Which year is famously known as the "Year of Great Divide" in the demographic history of India because population growth began steadily rising after it?
explanation: The Census of 1921 is known as the "Year of Great Divide" because prior to 1921 India had fluctuating population growth due to famines, after which it showed constant upward growth.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 7: Indian Economy, Section 7.4

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (1991 Reforms)
question: Who was the Finance Minister of India who introduced the landmark New Economic Policy (LPG: Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) in July 1991?
explanation: Dr. Manmohan Singh served as Union Finance Minister in P.V. Narasimha Rao’s cabinet when the historic 1991 economic reforms budget was delivered.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 8: Indian Economy, Section 8.2

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Fiscal)
question: Under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India at the expiration of every:
explanation: Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission every fifth year or earlier to recommend the sharing of tax revenues between Union and States.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Economics, Lesson 9: Fiscal Economics, Section 9.6

subject: History
lessonTitle: Society and Culture in Ancient Tamizhagam: The Sangam Age
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Sangam Age
question: The royal emblem of the Chera rulers during the ancient Sangam Age was the:
explanation: During the Sangam period: Cheras had the Bow and Arrow, Cholas had the Tiger, and Pandyas had the Double Fish (Carp) as their royal crest.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 6 Social Science, Term 3, History Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Tamil & History
lessonTitle: Thirukkural: Secular Philosophy and Everyday Conduct
topic: Structure and Universal Human Values of Thirukkural
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Thirukkural
question: The Thirukkural by Thiruvalluvar is classified into three divisions (Arathuppal, Porutpal, Kammathuppal) comprising how many total chapters (Adhikarams) and couplets (Kurals)?
explanation: Thirukkural consists of 133 Adhikarams, each containing 10 Kurals, totaling 1,330 couplets across Aram (38), Porul (70), and Inbam (25).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Tamil & Social Science, Unit 3: Thirukkural

subject: History
lessonTitle: The Justice Party and Non-Brahmin Movement
topic: Midday Meal Scheme & Justice Party Firsts
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Justice Party Governance
question: In 1920, the Justice Party government under Sir P. Theagaraya Chetty introduced the pioneer Midday Meal scheme in corporation schools of which city?
explanation: The Madras Corporation under Mayor Sir P. Theagaraya Chetty introduced a free school lunch scheme for poor children at Thousand Lights, Madras in 1920.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.2

subject: History
lessonTitle: The Dravidian Movement and Perarignar Anna
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Dravidian Administration
question: In 1967, Chief Minister C.N. Annadurai legalised Self-Respect Marriages (Suyamariyadhai Thirumanam) without priestly rituals by amending which act?
explanation: The Hindu Marriage (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act 1967 inserted Section 7-A into the Hindu Marriage Act 1955, granting full legal recognition to Self-Respect Marriages.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.6

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: What is the absolute zero temperature on the Celsius scale at which all molecular motion ceases?
explanation: Absolute zero corresponds to 0 Kelvin or -273.15 °C, the theoretical temperature at which thermal motion of particles ceases.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 7 Science, Term 1, Lesson 1: Heat and Temperature

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: What is the audible frequency range of sound waves capable of being detected by a normal human ear?
explanation: The audible sonic range for normal human hearing is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Frequencies below 20 Hz are infrasonic, and above 20 kHz are ultrasonic.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Science, Lesson 6: Sound, Section 6.3

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: Which gas is the most abundant component in the Earth’s atmosphere by volume?
explanation: Dry air in the atmosphere comprises roughly 78.08% Nitrogen, 20.95% Oxygen, 0.93% Argon, and 0.04% Carbon Dioxide.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Science, Lesson 10: Air, Section 10.1

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: What is the value of escape velocity required for an object to break free from the gravitational pull of the Earth without further propulsion?
explanation: Escape velocity from the surface of Earth is ve = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Physics, Volume 2, Lesson 6: Gravitation, Section 6.4

subject: Chemistry
lessonTitle: Basic Concepts of Chemistry and Chemical Calculations
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: What is the exact numerical value of the Avogadro constant (NA), representing the number of particles in one mole of a substance?
explanation: Avogadro’s constant is defined as 6.022 × 10²³ entities per mole of substance.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Chemistry, Volume 1, Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Botany
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Botany)
question: Which non-membrane bound cellular organelle is the universal site of protein synthesis in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
explanation: Ribosomes (70S in prokaryotes, 80S in eukaryotes) translate mRNA into polypeptide chains (proteins).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Bio-Botany, Lesson 6: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 6.5

subject: Zoology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Zoology)
question: In human females, where in the reproductive tract does natural fertilization of the ovum by a sperm typically occur?
explanation: Fertilization normally takes place in the ampullary region of the Fallopian (uterine) tube.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Bio-Zoology, Lesson 2: Human Reproduction, Section 2.4

subject: Zoology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Zoology)
question: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium and transmitted to humans through the bite of which vector?
explanation: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito carrying Plasmodium sporozoites.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Bio-Zoology, Lesson 7: Human Health and Diseases, Section 7.2

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: Nuclear fission in Uranium-235 was first discovered by which scientists in 1938?
explanation: German chemists Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann discovered nuclear fission of uranium when bombarded with thermal neutrons in 1938.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 6: Nuclear Physics, Section 6.2

subject: Chemistry
topic: Modern Periodic Table Groups and Periods
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: In the Modern Periodic Table, how many horizontal periods and vertical groups are present?
explanation: The modern periodic table consists of 7 horizontal rows called periods and 18 vertical columns called groups.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 8: Periodic Classification, Section 8.1

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: Which maritime channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal?
explanation: The Ten Degree (10°) Channel separates the Andaman archipelago to the north from the Nicobar archipelago to the south.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 1, Section 1.4

subject: Geography
topic: Cropping Seasons of India (Kharif, Rabi, Zaid)
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: Which cropping season in India begins with the onset of the Southwest Monsoon in June and is harvested in September–October?
explanation: Kharif crops (e.g., rice, cotton, maize, groundnut) are sown with the onset of monsoon in June and harvested in autumn (Sept-Oct).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 3, Section 3.3

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India
question: Which Indian state is the largest producer of Bauxite (aluminium ore) in India, accounting for over half of the national output?
explanation: Odisha is the leading bauxite-producing state in India, with deposits concentrated in the Kalahandi and Koraput belts.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 4, Section 4.1

subject: Geography
topic: Coastal Plains & Beaches of Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: Marina Beach in Chennai, along the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, is ranked as the:
options: Longest natural urban beach in the world
Second longest natural urban beach in the world
Largest tidal flat beach in India
explanation: Marina Beach stretching approximately 13 km along Chennai’s coast is recognized as the world’s second longest urban beach (after Miami Beach).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 6, Section 6.4

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: The Pichavaram Mangrove Forest, one of the largest in India, is situated near Chidambaram in which district of Tamil Nadu?
explanation: Pichavaram mangrove wetland is situated near Killai in Cuddalore district, between the Vellar and Coleroon (Kollidam) estuaries.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 6, Section 6.6

subject: Geography
topic: Cropping Calendar of Tamil Nadu (Samba, Kuruvai)
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: In the agricultural calendar of the Cauvery delta in Tamil Nadu, the long-duration winter rice crop sown in July–August and harvested in January is called:
explanation: Samba is the major rice season in Tamil Nadu (sown in July/August and harvested in January during Pongal), having a 5 to 6-month growth cycle.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 7, Section 7.2

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Medieval India
question: Who laid the foundation of the Qutb Minar in Delhi in 1199 AD in honour of the Sufi saint Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki?
explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, founder of the Slave Dynasty, began construction of the Qutb Minar, which was later completed by his successor Iltutmish.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 7 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 3, Section 3.2

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Medieval India
question: Which Delhi Sultan instituted strict market control regulations and appointed an officer called "Shahna-i-Mandi" to regulate commodity prices?
explanation: Alauddin Khalji fixed the prices of essential commodities, grains, and horses and established state granaries to maintain a large army at low cost.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 7 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 3, Section 3.4

subject: History
lessonTitle: Vijayanagar and Bahmani Kingdoms: Polity & Arts
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Medieval South India
question: The Vijayanagar Empire was founded on the banks of the Tungabhadra River in 1336 by which two brothers inspired by Saint Vidyaranya?
options: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I
explanation: Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty founded Vijayanagar in 1336 with their spiritual guru Vidyaranya’s blessings.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 7 Social Science, Term 2, History Lesson 1, Section 1.1

subject: History
lessonTitle: Vijayanagar and Bahmani Kingdoms: Polity & Arts
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Medieval South India
question: The historic Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi Tangadi) in 1565 led to the decisive defeat and destruction of which great South Indian empire?
explanation: In 1565, the combined Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, Bidar) defeated the Vijayanagar army led by Rama Raya at Talikota.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 7 Social Science, Term 2, History Lesson 1, Section 1.4

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: On 29 March 1857, which sepoy at Barrackpore cantonment refused to use the greased cartridge and attacked his British adjutant?
explanation: Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry mutinied at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and was executed on 8 April 1857.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 5, Section 5.1

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: During the 1857 Revolt, Begum Hazrat Mahal led the rebel forces against the British from which prominent city in Awadh?
explanation: Begum Hazrat Mahal took charge of Lucknow, proclaimed her minor son Birjis Qadr as Nawab, and resisted the British siege until 1858.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 5, Section 5.3

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: The historic Poona Pact of September 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to resolve the controversy surrounding:
options: Communal Award and separate electorates for Depressed Classes
explanation: The Poona Pact replaced Ramsay MacDonald’s separate electorates with reserved seats for depressed classes within joint electorates.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 8, Section 8.6

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Freedom Struggle in Tamil Nadu
question: Which young freedom fighter from Tamil Nadu embraced martyrdom holding the national tricolour flag aloft during a police lathi charge at Tiruppur in 1932?
explanation: Kumaran refused to let the Indian national flag touch the ground even when brutally beaten to death by the police, earning the title "Kodi Kaatha Kumaran".
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 9, Section 9.4

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Citizenship)
question: Under the Citizenship Act of 1955, in how many distinct ways can Indian citizenship be acquired?
explanation: Indian citizenship can be acquired in 5 ways: Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, and Incorporation of Territory.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.2

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Writs)
question: Which constitutional writ literally translates from Latin as "To have the body of" and protects individuals against unlawful detention?
explanation: Habeas Corpus is an order directing the detaining authority to produce the arrested person before court to test the legality of detention.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Emergency Provisions)
question: Under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, the President can declare a National Emergency on grounds of:
options: War, external aggression, or armed rebellion
Failure of constitutional machinery in a state
explanation: Article 352 provides for National Emergency on grounds of War, External Aggression, or Armed Rebellion (the term "armed rebellion" replaced "internal disturbance" via the 44th Amendment Act 1978).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.6

subject: Polity
topic: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (CAG)
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, designated as the guardian of the public purse?
explanation: Article 148 establishes the independent constitutional office of the CAG of India, who audits all receipts and expenditures of Union and State governments.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.6

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Attorney General)
question: Who is the highest law officer in the Government of India appointed under Article 76 of the Constitution?
explanation: The Attorney General for India (Article 76) is the chief legal adviser to the Union Government and has the right of audience in all Indian courts.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.4

subject: Polity
lessonTitle: Constitution of India: Framing & Basic Structure
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Basic Structure)
question: The landmark "Basic Structure Doctrine" limiting the amending power of Parliament under Article 368 was established by the Supreme Court in which case?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), a 13-judge constitutional bench ruled that Parliament cannot alter or destroy the basic structure of the Constitution under Article 368.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Political Science, Lesson 1: Constitution of India, Section 1.5

subject: Polity
lessonTitle: Election Commission and Electoral System in India
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Elections)
question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the superintendence, direction, and control of elections vested in the Election Commission of India?
explanation: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction, and conduct of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Political Science, Lesson 3, Section 3.2

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Employment in India and Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Labour)
question: What percentage of the total workforce in India is approximately engaged in the informal (unorganized) sector?
explanation: More than 90% of India’s working population is employed in the unorganized sector without formal social security benefits.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Social Science, Economics Lesson 2, Section 2.3

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Gross Domestic Product and Sectoral Contributions
topic: Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (National Income)
question: National Income of a country is formally defined as which macroeconomic aggregate?
options: Gross Domestic Product at Market Price (GDP_MP)
Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNP_FC)
Gross National Product at Factor Cost (GNP_FC)
explanation: National Income (NI) is strictly measured as Net National Product at Factor Cost: NNP_FC = GNP - Depreciation - Net Indirect Taxes.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 1, Section 1.4

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Indian Economy Before and After Independence
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Planning)
question: India’s First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956) was based on which economic growth model focusing heavily on agriculture and irrigation?
explanation: The First 5-Year Plan was formulated on the Harrod-Domar growth model and emphasized dam construction (Bhakra-Nangal, Hirakud) and agriculture.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 8: Indian Economy, Section 8.4

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Privatisation)
question: The sale of government-owned equity shares in Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) to private investors and the public is termed as:
explanation: Disinvestment refers to the dilution or sale of government shareholding in public sector undertakings to mobilize resources and enhance efficiency.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 8: Indian Economy, Section 8.6

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Tamil Nadu Economy: Macro Performance & HDI
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Tamil Nadu Economy
question: The Muppandal Wind Farm, one of the world’s largest operational onshore wind farms, is located in which district of Tamil Nadu?
explanation: Muppandal wind farm near Aralvaimozhi pass in Kanyakumari district generates over 1,500 MW of renewable wind energy, making Tamil Nadu a national leader.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 11: Tamil Nadu Economy, Section 11.4

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Inflation)
question: Inflation caused by an increase in input costs such as wages of labour, raw materials, or crude oil prices is classified as:
explanation: Cost-Push inflation occurs when aggregate supply decreases due to higher production costs (rising wages, raw material prices), pushing up general prices.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Economics, Lesson 5: Monetary Economics, Section 5.3

subject: History
lessonTitle: Ancient Ports and Cities of Tamilagam
topic: Ancient Port of Korkai & Pearl Fishery
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Ancient Tamil Ports
question: Which ancient Pandya port city situated at the mouth of the Thamirabarani River was world-famous for its natural pearl fisheries mentioned in Megasthenes’ accounts?
explanation: Korkai in present-day Thoothukudi district was the renowned ancient port and pearl capital of the early Pandya dynasty.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 6 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 4, Section 4.2

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Chola Architecture
question: The majestic Brihadisvara Temple (Peruvudaiyar Kovil) at Thanjavur was consecrated in 1010 CE by which great Chola emperor?
explanation: Rajaraja Chola I built the grand monolithic granite vimana of Brihadisvara temple in Thanjavur, completing it around 1010 CE.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 7 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 1, Section 1.2

subject: History
lessonTitle: People Revolt: Poligar Rebellion & 1806 Vellore Mutiny
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Freedom Fighters of Tamil Nadu
question: Which courageous Kongu chieftain allied with Tipu Sultan waged guerrilla warfare against the British and was hanged at Sankagiri Fort in July 1805?
explanation: Dheeran Chinnamalai (Theerthagiri) fought the British East India Company at Cauvery, Odanilai, and Arachalur before being betrayed and hanged at Sankagiri on 31 July 1805.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 4, Section 4.4

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Pure Tamil Movement (Thani Tamizh Iyakkam)
question: Swami Vedachalam, a profound Tamil scholar who changed his name into pure Tamil, is venerated as the father of the Pure Tamil Movement (தனித்தமிழ் இயக்கம்). What was his Tamil name?
explanation: Swami Vedachalam founded the Pure Tamil Movement (1916) and adopted the pure Tamil name Maraimalai Adigal, renaming his journal "Gnanachagaram" to "Arivukkadal".
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.2

subject: History

subject: Ethics and Culture

explanation: Keeladi in Sivagangai district, located 12 km southeast of Madurai on the Vaigai river plains, has yielded brick structures, ring wells, and Tamil-Brahmi sherds dating to 6th Century BCE.

subject: History
lessonTitle: The Justice Party Ministries & Affirmative Policies

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 History, Lesson 5, Section 5.3

subject: Biology
lessonTitle: Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood group system in 1900. Which blood group is known as the "Universal Donor" because it has neither A nor B antigens on RBCs?
explanation: Blood Group O lacks both A and B antigens on red blood cell membranes, preventing agglutination when transfused into any recipient.

subject: Chemistry

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: Which of the following is an example of a conservative force where work done is independent of the path taken?

subject: Geography

tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 6, Section 6.5

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: India’s largest open-cast brown coal (Lignite) mining and thermal power complex is operated by NLC India Limited at Neyveli in which district of Tamil Nadu?

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 7, Section 7.3

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Physical Geography

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Social Science, Geography Lesson 4, Section 4.4

subject: History

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 7, Section 7.3

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: Following which violent incident in Gorakhpur district on 5 February 1922 did Mahatma Gandhi abruptly suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement?
explanation: At Chauri Chaura, an angry crowd burnt down a police station killing 22 policemen. Appalled by the violence, Gandhi called off Non-Cooperation on 12 Feb 1922.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 8, Section 8.3

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: At the All-India Congress Committee session in Gowalia Tank, Bombay on 8 August 1942, Mahatma Gandhi gave which iconic call to the nation?
options: "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom"

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 8, Section 8.7

subject: History
topic: Vanchi Nathan & Ashe Murder at Maniyachi
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Freedom Struggle in Tamil Nadu
question: On 17 June 1911, Vanchi Nathan shot dead Robert Ashe, the Collector of Tirunelveli, at which railway junction before shooting himself?
explanation: Vanchi Nathan of the Bharatha Matha Association assassinated Collector Ashe at Maniyachi railway station to avenge the repression of Swadeshi leaders.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 9, Section 9.3

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Fundamental Rights)
question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the practice of "Untouchability" abolished and its practice in any form made a punishable offence?
explanation: Article 17 of the Constitution of India unconditionally abolishes Untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Fundamental Rights)
question: Article 21-A, which makes free and compulsory education for all children between 6 and 14 years a Fundamental Right, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
explanation: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002 inserted Article 21-A into Part III of the Constitution.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.4

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Judiciary)
question: The Madras High Court, one of the three oldest High Courts in India established in 1862, possesses a permanent principal bench at Chennai and a circuit bench at:

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 3, Section 3.6

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Food Security and Universal PDS in Tamil Nadu
topic: K. Kamaraj Midday Meal Scheme Expansion
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Tamil Nadu Welfare Schemes
question: Which visionary Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu introduced the free statewide Midday Meal Scheme in primary schools in 1956 to boost student enrolment and eradicate classroom hunger?
explanation: Chief Minister K. Kamaraj pioneered the free School Noon Meals scheme in 1956 across all primary schools in Tamil Nadu, which became a model for all India.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 3, Section 3.4

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Tamil Nadu Economy
question: Which town in southern Tamil Nadu, affectionately termed "Kutti Japan" (Little Japan) by Jawaharlal Nehru, produces over 80% of India’s safety matches and fireworks?
explanation: Sivakasi in Virudhunagar district dominates the printing, matchbox, and pyrotechnics industries, earning the moniker "Little Japan".
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 5, Section 5.3

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Indian Economy Before and After Independence
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Agriculture)
question: Which world-renowned agricultural scientist from Tamil Nadu is venerated as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for introducing High Yielding Varieties (HYV) of wheat and rice?
explanation: M.S. Swaminathan collaborated with Norman Borlaug to introduce semi-dwarf high-yielding Mexican wheat and rice varieties into India during the 1960s.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 8, Section 8.3

subject: History
lessonTitle: Society and Culture in Ancient Tamizhagam: The Sangam Age
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Tamil Literature & Epics
question: The twin great Tamil epics "Silappathikaram" and "Manimekalai" were authored respectively by:
explanation: Prince-ascetic Ilango Adigal wrote Silappathikaram (the story of Kannagi and Kovalan), and Buddhist merchant-poet Seethalai Sathanar composed Manimekalai.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10 & Class 6 Term 3, Section 1.5

subject: History
lessonTitle: Early Tamil Society, Epigraphy and Archaeological Discoveries
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Archaeological Excavations in TN
question: The prehistoric Iron Age megalithic urn-burial site excavated by Dr. Jagor (1876) and Alexander Rea along the Thamirabarani basin in Tamil Nadu is:
explanation: Adichanallur in Thoothukudi district is an extensive urn burial (Megalithic) site containing iron implements, bronze artifacts, and gold diadems.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Social Science, History Lesson 3, Section 3.5

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Social Reformers of Tamil Nadu
question: For leading the 1924 agitation against untouchability and securing temple entry road access in Travancore, Periyar E.V. Ramasamy was honoured with the title:
explanation: Periyar was imprisoned twice during the Vaikom Satyagraha in Travancore, and his relentless struggle earned him the title "Vaikom Veerar" (Hero of Vaikom) from Thiru. Vi. Ka.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.4

subject: History
lessonTitle: The Dravidian Movement and Perarignar Anna
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Dravidian Movement Governance
question: In January 1968, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly under Chief Minister C.N. Annadurai passed a historic resolution eliminating Hindi and officially adopting which language policy in state schools?
explanation: C.N. Annadurai eliminated the Three-Language Formula and institutionalized the Two-Language Formula (Tamil and English) in the curriculum of Tamil Nadu schools.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.6

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double-helical structure of DNA in 1953. In DNA, adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T) via how many hydrogen bonds?
explanation: According to Chargaff’s base-pairing rules, Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine (A = T), and Guanine forms three hydrogen bonds with Cytosine (G ≡ C).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 18: Genetics, Section 18.5

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: What is the chemical name and formula of Baking Soda commonly used in cooking and antacids?
explanation: Baking soda is Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3); washing soda is Sodium Carbonate Decahydrate (Na2CO3·10H2O).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 10, Section 10.5

subject: Physics
topic: Newton’s Third Law of Motion & Rocket Propulsion
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: The propulsion of space rockets in atmosphere and outer space operates on the principle of:
options: Newton’s Third Law and Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum
Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation alone
Kepler’s Third Law of Planetary Motion
explanation: Rocket propulsion is based on Newton’s 3rd law (for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction) and the law of conservation of linear momentum.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 1: Laws of Motion, Section 1.8

subject: Geography
topic: Minerals of Tamil Nadu (Magnesite in Salem)
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: The Chalk Hills of Salem district in Tamil Nadu hold world-class reserves of which vital industrial mineral used in refractory bricks?
explanation: The Chalk Hills of Salem contain vast deposits of Magnesite (MgCO3) mined by Tamil Nadu Magnesite Limited (TANMAG) for refractory linings.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 7, Section 7.3

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: The coastal beach placer sands of Kanyakumari and Tirunelveli districts are rich in Monazite, which is an important source of which nuclear fuel?
explanation: Monazite beach sand contains high concentrations of Thorium phosphate, mined by Indian Rare Earths Limited (IREL) at Manavalakurichi.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 7, Section 7.3

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Physical Geography
question: Rocks that are formed through the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava are designated as:
explanation: Igneous rocks (from Latin ignis = fire) are called primary rocks because all other rock types are ultimately derived from them.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Social Science, Geography Lesson 1, Section 1.2

subject: History
lessonTitle: Rural Life and Society: Colonial Land Tenures
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Colonial Land Revenue
question: The Ryotwari land revenue system, where revenue settlement was made directly with individual cultivator-peasants (ryots), was introduced in the Madras Presidency in 1820 by:

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 8 Social Science, Term 1, History Lesson 3, Section 3.2

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Indian National Movement
question: Why was the statutory Indian Statutory Commission (Simon Commission) appointed in November 1927 unanimously boycotted by Indian political parties?
options: It was an all-white commission without a single Indian member
It recommended the partition of India
It banned the Indian National Congress
It refused to visit southern states

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 8, Section 8.4

subject: History
lessonTitle: Anti-Colonial Movements and Birth of Nationalism
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: 19th Century Movements
question: In which year did the Wahabi Movement’s major confrontation against British authority culminate under the leadership of Titu Mir in Bengal?
explanation: Titu Mir led the anti-British peasant struggle in Bengal, constructing a bamboo fortress at Narkelberia, where he fell fighting British troops in 1831.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 7, Section 7.2

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Article 19)
question: How many fundamental democratic freedoms are guaranteed to citizens of India under Article 19(1) of the Constitution?
explanation: Article 19 guarantees 6 freedoms (speech & expression, peaceful assembly, forming associations/unions, free movement, residence, and trade/occupation). Right to property was removed by 44th CAA.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Amendment)
question: In which Part and Article of the Constitution of India is the power and procedure for amending the Constitution laid down?
explanation: Part XX (Article 368) grants Parliament the constituent power to amend any provision of the Constitution by following the specified procedures.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.7

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (President)
question: What is the minimum age prescribed by the Indian Constitution under Article 58 for a candidate to contest the election for the President of India?
explanation: A presidential candidate must be a citizen of India, have completed 35 years of age, and be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.1

subject: Economics
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Employment)
question: The phenomenon in Indian agriculture where more people are engaged in a farm activity than strictly required, such that marginal productivity of additional labour is zero, is termed:
explanation: Disguised unemployment (underemployment) occurs when labour productivity at the margin is zero or negligible, typical of family farms in rural India.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 Economics, Lesson 10, Section 10.3

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Banking and Central Banking: Reserve Bank of India
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Indian Economy (Banking)
question: How many major private commercial banks with deposits over ₹50 crore were nationalised by the Government of India in the first phase on 19 July 1969?
explanation: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 major private commercial banks on 19 July 1969 to direct credit toward agriculture and priority sectors.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Economics, Lesson 6, Section 6.3

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Food Security and Universal PDS in Tamil Nadu
tag: Group 1 • Unit V: Tamil Nadu Welfare Schemes
question: In July 1982, Chief Minister M.G. Ramachandran revolutionized child welfare in Tamil Nadu by launching the expanded:

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Economics Lesson 3, Section 3.4

subject: History
lessonTitle: Pioneers of Freedom Struggle in Tamil Nadu

tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Freedom Fighters of Tamil Nadu
question: Which courageous teenage Tamil girl from Mayiladuthurai participated in Mahatma Gandhi’s South African Satyagraha in 1913 and died at age 16 upon release from prison?
explanation: Thillaiyadi Valliammai endured brutal prison labour in South Africa, inspiring Mahatma Gandhi to describe her as one of his greatest moral inspirations in "Satyagraha in South Africa".
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 9, Section 9.1

subject: History
lessonTitle: Early Tamil Society, Epigraphy and Archaeological Discoveries
