explanation: The Uttiramerur Inscriptions (dated 919 and 921 CE) in Kanchipuram district detail qualifications, disqualifications, and the pot-ticket election system for village sabha committees.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10 & Class 7 Term 1, Section 1.3

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Dravidian Movement & Anna
question: Which Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu officiated the very first legalised Self-Respect Marriage in Chennai in 1967 without Vedic rituals or mangalsutra priests?
explanation: Perarignar C.N. Annadurai prioritized and passed the Hindu Marriage (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act 1967, granting full validity to Suyamariyadhai marriages.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.6

subject: Biology
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Biology)
question: Which of the following cellular features is characteristically absent in prokaryotic organisms such as bacteria?
explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack a defined membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 9 Science, Lesson 18: Cell Biology, Section 18.2

subject: Physics
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Physics)
question: According to Snell’s Law of Refraction, for light traveling from medium 1 to medium 2, the ratio of sin(i) to sin(r) is equal to:
explanation: Snell’s law states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant and equal to the ratio of refractive indices: sin(i)/sin(r) = μ2/μ1.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 2: Optics, Section 2.1

subject: Chemistry
tag: Group 1 • Unit I: General Science (Chemistry)
question: A solution where any liquid other than water acts as the solvent (such as benzene, ether, or carbon tetrachloride) is termed a:
explanation: Solutions in which water is the solvent are aqueous solutions; solutions in which solvents other than water are used are non-aqueous solutions.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Science, Lesson 9: Solutions, Section 9.1

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of India (Transport)
question: The very first passenger railway line in India was flagged off on 16 April 1853 between which two stations over a distance of 34 km?
explanation: India’s first train operated between Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane on 16 April 1853 under Lord Dalhousie.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 5, Section 5.3

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: Tamil Nadu is the only state in India having three major seaports. Which are the three major ports located in Tamil Nadu?

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 7, Section 7.5

subject: Geography
tag: Group 1 • Unit II: Geography of Tamil Nadu
question: What is the highest mountain peak situated within the geographical boundaries of Tamil Nadu in the Nilgiri Hills?
explanation: Doddabetta (2,637 metres) in the Nilgiri Hills is the highest peak in Tamil Nadu. (Anaimudi at 2,695 m is in Kerala).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Geography Lesson 6, Section 6.2

subject: History
lessonTitle: Cultural Syncretism and Bhakti Movement in India
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Bhakti Movement
question: Which 15th-century mystic poet and weaver from Varanasi composed devotional rhyming couplets (Dohas) collected in the "Bijak"?
explanation: Sant Kabir stressed the unity of God (Ishwar and Allah), rejected caste distinctions and ritualism, and his verses are compiled in the Bijak.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 11 History, Volume 2, Lesson 13, Section 13.3

subject: History

question: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose formed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) in October 1943 at:

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 8, Section 8.8

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit III: Swadeshi Movement in Tamil Nadu
question: V.O. Chidambaranar purchased two steamships, "S.S. Galia" and "S.S. Lavo", to sail between which two ports in challenge to the British monopoly?
explanation: Kappalottiya Thamizhan V.O.C. launched the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in 1906 plying ships between Tuticorin and Colombo.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 9, Section 9.2

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Fundamental Rights)
question: Which Article of the Constitution guarantees to every individual freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise, and propagate religion?
explanation: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 1, Section 1.3

subject: Polity
topic: Casting Vote of the Speaker of Lok Sabha
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Lok Sabha Speaker)
question: Under Article 100(1) of the Constitution, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha exercises a casting vote in which specific circumstance?
options: In the first instance on every ordinary bill
Only in the case of an equality of votes (tie)
explanation: The Speaker does not vote in the first instance, but exercises a casting vote under Article 100 to resolve an equality of votes (deadlock/tie).
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, Civics Lesson 2, Section 2.3

subject: Polity
tag: Group 1 • Unit IV: Indian Polity (Seventh Schedule)
question: In the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, on subjects listed under the Concurrent List (List III), who has the power to legislate?

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Government and Taxes: Fiscal Systems & GST

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Tamil Nadu Economy: Macro Performance & HDI

question: Which statutory corporation was established by the Government of Tamil Nadu in 1971 to develop industrial estates and provide financial assistance to large industries?

subject: Economics
lessonTitle: Economics of Development, Planning & NITI Aayog

sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 12 Economics, Lesson 11, Section 11.4

subject: History
tag: Group 1 • Unit VI: Women Leaders of Tamil Nadu
question: Which prominent Tamil social reformer and writer authored the novel "Dasigalin Mosavalai" (Web of Deceit of the Devadasis) exposed temple prostitution?
explanation: Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar crusaded against the Devadasi system and authored "Dasigalin Mosavalai" (1936). The TN marriage assistance scheme was named in her honour.
sourceReference: Samacheer Kalvi Class 10 Social Science, History Lesson 10, Section 10.7

subject: History

Periyar E.V. Ramasamy and C.N. Annadurai
